version: v1 for owner review (professor and CCO review fixes applied 22 Nov 2026)
label: Model policy for training - not for live lending decisions.

deals.RD-RES-01: Maple Run (Ohio), fix-and-flip to DSCR refinance
deals.RD-MF-01: Cedar Court (North Carolina), value-add bridge to agency take-out
deals.RD-COM-01: Birchwood Plaza (Indiana), retail bridge to bank take-out
deals.CAP-01: Capstone ground-up construction deal (fourth, unseen deal; not yet authored)

documents.name: Rent roll
documents.what_it_is: A list of every unit or suite with its tenant, lease dates and rent, as of one date.
documents.producer: Borrower or its property manager, exported from property management software. The lender ties it to leases and bank deposits.

format.description: Spreadsheet or PDF export. Multifamily rolls list units; commercial rolls list suites and lease terms. No single industry form.
references: Agency multifamily lenders publish their own rent roll templates [VERIFY: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac multifamily rent roll forms; not yet checked]

For 2-4 unit residential collateral, rent data sits in the appraisal: legacy Fannie Mae Form 1025, now the redesigned URAR Small Residential Income report [VERIFY: Freddie Mac UAD and forms redesign FAQ; checked 22 Nov 2026]

fields_to_read: As-of date, and whether it matches the T-12 end date
Unit or suite, type and square feet
Status: occupied, vacant, notice, model, down
Tenant name, lease start and end, move-in date
Market rent and contract rent; concessions and free rent
Commercial only: base rent per square foot, escalations, recovery type (NNN, modified gross, gross), renewal options, share of total rent
planted_defects: Rent roll collections do not tie to bank deposits within the MF-GEN-04 tolerance for the last 3 months (fake rent roll).
Occupied units include model, down or long-delinquent units, so physical occupancy overstates economic occupancy.
Contract rent shown gross of concessions; free months appear only in the lease file.
A lease end date disagrees with the lease or estoppel (Birchwood: the largest tenant's lease ends in month 20).
Several new leases signed in the last 60 days at rents above the rest of the roll, to tenants with no deposit.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: 44 of 50 units leased (88%); GPR $780,000; rent-roll collections annualized $702,000; trailing 3 months annualized $708,000. Birchwood Plaza: 11 suites, 28,000 of 40,000 sf leased (70%); base rent $420,000; largest tenant $90,000, lease ends month 20; $150,000 of rent expires within 24 months.

formulas_fed.input: rent roll total, compared with deposits

documents.input_rule: Multifamily income is the lesser of rent-roll collections annualized and trailing 3 months annualized (MF-GEN-05): Cedar Court $702,000, not $708,000. Commercial rent is checked against leases and estoppels; where they differ, the lease and estoppel control and the difference is a finding (COM-GEN-09).
documents.data_needed: Unit-level Cedar Court rows (unit mix, rents, concessions) and suite-level Birchwood rows that sum to the deal totals. Not in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: T-12 operating statement
documents.what_it_is: Twelve months of income and expenses, month by month, for the property.
documents.producer: Borrower or property manager, from the property's books. The underwriter normalizes it to underwritten NOI.

format.description: Spreadsheet with 12 monthly columns and a total. Cash or accrual basis, which the statement should state.
references: Fannie Mae Form 216, Operating Income Statement, for 2-4 unit residential [VERIFY: Fannie Mae Selling Guide forms page; not yet checked]
CREFC Investor Reporting Package Operating Statement Analysis Report as the normalization layout in CMBS [VERIFY: CREFC IRP v8.4, Mar 2024; crefc.org; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Period covered and basis (cash or accrual)
Income lines: rent, vacancy loss, concessions, other income, recoveries
Expense lines: taxes, insurance, utilities, repairs, payroll, management, general and administrative
Items that are capital, one-time or non-cash
Monthly pattern: seasonality and late-year jumps
NOI line and whether it ties to the monthly columns
planted_defects: One-time income left in revenue, such as an insurance recovery or a lease termination fee.
Capital work booked as repairs, or repairs capitalized below the NOI line.
Taxes at the seller's old assessment and insurance at the old premium, with no reset for the sale.
Cash-basis statement that omits an unpaid tax installment, so expenses are understated.
Management fee missing or below the family floor (MF-GEN-06; COM-GEN-06).
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: T-12 expenses $298,000; appraiser $310,000; other income $18,000; taxes $74,000 and insurance $38,000 a year. Birchwood Plaza: T-12 expenses $196,000; appraiser $204,000; recoveries $84,000.
documents.input_rule: Expenses are the greater of the T-12 and the appraiser's estimate (MF-GEN-06; COM-GEN-06): Cedar Court $310,000, Birchwood $204,000.
documents.data_needed: Monthly line items for both deals that sum to the stated totals.

documents.name: Appraisal excerpt
documents.what_it_is: Key pages of the appraiser's report: value conclusions, premises, approaches, comparables and certification.
documents.producer: State-certified appraiser engaged by the lender through an appraisal management company (CORE-VAL-01). MAI-designated for multifamily and commercial (MF-GEN-08; COM-GEN-13).

format.description: 1-4 unit: the redesigned Uniform Residential Appraisal Report, with a rental section. Income property: a narrative report.
references: Redesigned URAR under UAD 3.6, mandatory for GSE submissions from 2 Nov 2026 [VERIFY: Fannie Mae UAD 3.6 FAQ; checked 22 Nov 2026; a later exception date was reported but not confirmed]

Single Family Comparable Rent Schedule (legacy Form 1007), now a URAR rental section; the legacy form is accepted only in limited cases [VERIFY: Freddie Mac UAD and forms redesign FAQ; checked 22 Nov 2026]
Federally related transactions: appraisals follow USPAP and the agencies' minimum standards [VERIFY: 12 CFR 34.44; not yet checked]. Our model lender is a non-bank, so this is a benchmark.

fields_to_read: Client and intended user (the lender, not the borrower)
Value premises: as-is, as-complete or as-stabilized, ARV
Income approach: NOI, cap rate, vacancy and expenses used
Sales comparison grid: dates, distance, condition, adjustments
Cost approach where used (new or heavily renovated property)
Market rent (residential rental section, or the commercial rent survey)
Reconciliation and final value; exposure time
planted_defects: Client is the borrower or a broker: a borrower-supplied appraisal is rejected (CORE-VAL-01).
Effective date more than 120 days before closing (CORE-VAL-02, F-CORE-36).
ARV comparables are unrenovated, outside the submarket, or listings rather than sales.
An as-stabilized value is presented as as-is, or a hypothetical condition is not disclosed.
Appraiser's NOI uses rents above the rent roll with no explanation.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: as-is $310,000; ARV $520,000; market rent $2,400 a month; effective 12 days before closing. Cedar Court: as-is $6,300,000; as-stabilized $8,600,000. Birchwood Plaza: as-is $4,500,000; as-stabilized $6,000,000; stabilized cap rate on NOI 8.00%.
documents.input_rule: Value is the lower of price and appraised as-is value (F-CORE-14): Maple Run $300,000, Cedar Court $6,200,000, Birchwood $4,400,000. DSCR rent is the lesser of lease rent and appraisal market rent (RES-DSCR-01, F-RES-23): Maple Run $2,400.
documents.data_needed: Comparable grids and approach detail for each deal. ARV and rent are labelled course assumptions in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Appraisal review (desk review)
documents.what_it_is: A second appraiser's or internal reviewer's check of whether the appraisal is credible and usable.
documents.producer: Internal review appraiser or third-party reviewer, independent of loan production (CORE-VAL-03).

format.description: Review memo or review form: scope, checks by approach, deficiencies, conclusion.
references: USPAP Standard 3 sets appraisal review development and reporting [VERIFY: USPAP current edition, The Appraisal Foundation; not yet checked]
Reviewer independence from production [VERIFY: Interagency Appraisal and Evaluation Guidelines, Section XV; cited in C5 blueprint; not yet checked here]

fields_to_read: Reviewer name, credential and reporting line
Scope: desk or field; report version and effective date reviewed
Checks on each approach and on the comparables
Deficiencies, each with its effect on value
Whether the reviewer states a value opinion of their own
planted_defects: Reviewer reports to the loan officer or was paid by production.
Review accepts a comparable that the appraisal excerpt shows is unrenovated or stale.
Review checks a different report version or effective date than the one in the file.
Review of a flip appraisal checks ARV but not the as-is value that sizes the day-one advance.
Review is dated after closing.
documents.deal_facts: Reviews the DOC-03 report for each deal. No review exists in the Running Deals tab.
documents.input_rule: Only a value the review accepts may enter a formula. A rejected appraisal leaves the value input blank, not estimated.
documents.data_needed: Review text and findings, written to match DOC-03.

documents.name: Purchase contract and chain of title
documents.what_it_is: The signed contract to buy the property, with any assignment, read against the recorded deeds.
documents.producer: Buyer and seller, often through brokers or a wholesaler. The title company supplies the deed history.

format.description: Purchase and sale agreement with addenda; assignment of contract; deed history from the title search.
references: No standard national form; state realtor forms are common for 1-4 units [VERIFY: Ohio REALTORS purchase contract; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Price, deposit, credits and seller concessions
Seller's acquisition date and price on the deed history
planted_defects: Assignment fee lifts the price well above the seller's recent purchase price (rapid flip chain).
Seller credits make the real price lower than the contract price.
Seller is related to the borrower, so the deal is not arm's length.
Buyer on the contract differs from the borrowing entity.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: $300,000 arm's-length contract with an unrelated seller. Cedar Court price $6,200,000. Birchwood Plaza price $4,400,000.
documents.input_rule: Price is the contract price net of seller credits. Where an assignment adds a fee, test value against the price paid by the end buyer and flag the chain.
documents.data_needed: Contract terms beyond price, and a deed history, for each deal.

documents.name: Credit report (tri-merge)
documents.what_it_is: A merged personal credit report on each guarantor, from the three national bureaus.
documents.producer: A credit reporting agency or reseller, pulled by the lender with a permissible purpose.

format.description: Tri-merge report: scores, identity, addresses, tradelines, public records, inquiries, alerts.
references: Permissible purpose for a report on a guarantor [VERIFY: 15 U.S.C. 1681b(a)(3)(A); cited in C6 blueprint; not yet checked here]

fields_to_read: Name, SSN match and address history
Current address versus the subject property
planted_defects: Report older than 90 days at closing (CORE-BOR-07).
Subject property shows as the guarantor's current address (occupancy red flag, CORE-BP-02).
Highest score used instead of the mid-score.
Mortgages on the report that are missing from the schedule of real estate owned.
Foreclosure or short sale inside 48 months (CORE-BOR-08), or an SSN mismatch alert.
documents.deal_facts: Dana Reyes 705 / 712 / 730 (mid 712); Sam Okafor 640 / 655 / 668 (mid 655). Marcus Hale mid 728; Priya Nand mid 702. Dana Whitlow mid 742; Leo Marsh mid 690.
documents.input_rule: Mid-score is the middle of three scores, or the lower of two (CORE-BOR-07). Liabilities on the PFS must include every debt on the credit report.
documents.data_needed: Tradelines and addresses for each guarantor. Only scores exist in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Background report
documents.what_it_is: A public-records search on each guarantor and the borrower: criminal, bankruptcy, foreclosure, liens, judgments, litigation.
documents.producer: A background search vendor, ordered by the lender (CORE-KYC-03).

format.description: Vendor report with search scope, lookback period, sources and hits.
references: Fair-chance hiring laws do not govern credit decisions, but state rules on criminal history should be checked [VERIFY: CORE-BOR-09 tag; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Subject identifiers: name, aliases, date of birth
Bankruptcy, foreclosure, deed in lieu, short sale
planted_defects: Search run on a name match with a different date of birth, or without aliases.
A lien shows as open with no release in the file (Maple Run: the 2019 lien is released; the file must prove it).
Active litigation or judgment over the CORE-BOR-10 threshold not resolved before closing.
Affiliated entity with a foreclosure that is missing from the track record.
Lookback shorter than 10 years, or the borrowing LLC was not searched.
documents.deal_facts: Dana Reyes: one $8,000 state tax lien, filed 2019, paid and released 2020; no bankruptcy, foreclosure, felony or open litigation. Sam Okafor: no adverse items.
documents.input_rule: Where the background report and the borrower's disclosure differ, the report controls until the borrower documents otherwise.
documents.data_needed: Report pages for each guarantor. Only Maple Run has background facts in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Operating agreement
documents.what_it_is: The borrowing LLC's governing contract: members, percentages, managers and authority.
documents.producer: Borrower's counsel; signed by the members. The lender's counsel reviews it.

format.description: LLC operating agreement under the state LLC act, with a borrowing resolution or consent.
references: Ohio Revised Code chapter 1706; N.C. G.S. chapter 57D; Indiana Code 23-18.1 [VERIFY: state code sites; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Managing member and authority to borrow and sign
planted_defects: Percentages differ from the application, hiding a 20% owner who must guarantee and be screened (CORE-BOR-03; CORE-KYC-01).
Signer lacks authority; the agreement needs a member consent that is missing.
Purpose clause is not real estate, or the entity is not single-purpose where required (CORE-BOR-02; COM-GEN-04).
Unsigned copy, or an older version with later amendments missing.
A member is a trust, with no look-through to the people behind it.
documents.deal_facts: Harborline Holdings LLC (Ohio, 2021): Dana Reyes 60%, Sam Okafor 40%. Cedar Court Partners LLC (NC SPE): Marcus Hale 60%, Priya Nand 40%. Birchwood Plaza LLC (Indiana SPE): Dana Whitlow 75%, Leo Marsh 25%.

formulas_fed.input: ownership share in each track-record entity

documents.input_rule: Ownership comes from the signed operating agreement, multiplied through each layer. The application is a claim to test, not a source.
documents.data_needed: Agreement text. Ownership percentages exist in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Good-standing certificate
documents.what_it_is: The state's certificate that the entity exists and is current on its filings.
documents.producer: The Secretary of State of the formation state (and of the property state, if different).

format.description: One-page state certificate with entity name, number, status and issue date.
references: Certificate names vary by state (good standing, existence) [VERIFY: Ohio, North Carolina and Indiana Secretary of State sites; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Foreign registration in the property state, if formed elsewhere
planted_defects: Name differs from the operating agreement or title commitment by a word or suffix.
Status is inactive, forfeited or revoked.
Entity formed in another state with no foreign registration in the property state.
Certificate issued for a similarly named, different entity.
documents.deal_facts: Harborline Holdings LLC is in good standing (Running Deals). The other two are newly formed SPEs.
documents.input_rule: Not a formula input. A gate for CORE-BOR-01 and CORE-CLS-01.
documents.data_needed: None beyond entity names. The policy has no age limit for this certificate (open item).

documents.name: Personal financial statement and schedule of real estate owned
documents.what_it_is: The guarantor's own statement of assets, liabilities and properties owned.
documents.producer: The guarantor, on the lender's form, signed and dated.

format.description: Lender PFS form with a schedule of real estate owned (SREO).
references: No federal form for private lenders. SBA Form 413 is a familiar public example [VERIFY: SBA Form 413; sba.gov; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: SREO: each property, ownership share, value, debt, payment, rent
planted_defects: Mortgages on the credit report are missing from the SREO.
Values on the SREO exceed recent purchase prices with no support.
Contingent liabilities left blank while the guarantor has guaranteed other loans.
Statement is unsigned or old (no policy age rule yet: P-C6-3).
documents.deal_facts: Dana Reyes: total assets $1,150,000; total liabilities $610,000. Marcus Hale net worth $6,800,000. Dana Whitlow net worth $5,200,000.
documents.input_rule: Liquid assets come from statements (DOC-11), not the PFS. The PFS supplies net worth, tested against the credit report and SREO.
documents.data_needed: SREO rows and contingent guaranties for Marcus Hale and Dana Whitlow (P-C6-4).

documents.name: Bank and brokerage statements
documents.what_it_is: The guarantor's two most recent monthly account statements, used to verify liquidity.
documents.producer: The guarantor's bank or broker; delivered by the guarantor or by a verification service.

format.description: Monthly statement PDF: account holder, period, balances, transactions.
references: No standard form. Direct verification services are market practice [VERIFY: market practice; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Large recent deposits and their source
planted_defects: Statements older than 60 days at closing, or only one month (CORE-BOR-13).
Fonts, totals or running balances do not add up (altered statement).
A large deposit days before the statement with no source (borrowed funds).
Account held by a different person or entity.
documents.deal_facts: Dana Reyes: cash $95,000; brokerage $40,000; vested 401(k) $60,000; unused HELOC $75,000. Marcus Hale: cash $650,000; securities $400,000. Dana Whitlow: cash $550,000; securities $300,000.
documents.input_rule: Unused credit lines count at zero (D-CORE-06). Securities and retirement balances take the F-CORE-24 haircut.
documents.data_needed: Statement pages that match the balances above.

documents.name: Ownership chart and OFAC screening record
documents.what_it_is: A chart of every ownership layer down to people, with the sanctions screening result for each.
documents.producer: Originator builds the chart; compliance runs and records the screening.

format.description: Org chart plus a screening log: name screened, list, date and time, result, resolution.
references: OFAC regulations and the 50 Percent Rule [VERIFY: 31 CFR Part 501; treasury.gov; cited in CORE-KYC-01; not yet checked here]
Beneficial ownership customer due diligence rule [VERIFY: 31 CFR 1010.230; CORE-KYC-02 tag; not yet checked here]

fields_to_read: Names screened, list version, date and time
Potential matches and how each was cleared
planted_defects: A middle layer is missing, so a 20% indirect owner is not screened.
Screening predates a name change or was not re-run before funding (CORE-KYC-01; CORE-CLS-03).
A potential match closed with no note of why it is a false positive.
Trust shown as owner with no trustee or beneficiary named.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court and Birchwood equity also comes from passive investors in a separate holding LLC; their percentages are not in the Running Deals tab.
documents.input_rule: The chart is built from operating agreements (DOC-08), never from the application alone.
documents.data_needed: Holding-LLC investor list for Cedar Court and Birchwood. F-CORE-38 and -39 are reserved for C7 and not yet defined.

documents.name: Wire instructions and funding request
documents.what_it_is: The closing agent's instructions for where the lender sends loan funds, and the request to release them.
documents.producer: Closing agent (title agent or attorney); verified by the lender's closer.

format.description: Letter or secure-portal instructions; the lender's funding request and callback record.
references: Name and account number mismatch: the beneficiary's bank may rely on the number [VERIFY: UCC 4A-207(b)(1); cited in C11 blueprint; not yet checked here]
ALTA closing protection letter [VERIFY: ALTA CPL form; cited in C11 blueprint; not yet checked here]

fields_to_read: Match to the CPL agent's escrow account
planted_defects: Instructions changed by email the day before funding.
Beneficiary name and account number belong to different parties.
Sender's email domain differs by one character from the agent's.
Callback made to the number in the email, not the number on file.
One person prepared and released the wire (CORE-CLS-03).
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run net funding wire $233,738.33 (F-CORE-41).
documents.input_rule: The wire amount must equal the settlement statement (DOC-28), not the funding request.
documents.data_needed: Agent names and fictional account details for each deal.

documents.name: Term sheet
documents.what_it_is: The lender's non-binding summary of proposed loan terms, issued before full underwriting.
documents.producer: Originator, from the lender's template; approved for issue by credit where required.

format.description: Two to four pages: parties, amount, advances, rate, fees, term, recourse, escrows, conditions, expiry.
references: No standard form. Non-binding language and a deposit clause are market practice [VERIFY: market practice; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Rate, index, spread, cap; points and fees
planted_defects: Cash to close does not add up (Maple Run $74,100; Cedar Court $2,240,066.67; Birchwood $1,735,200).
Points computed on the initial advance, not the commitment (F-CORE-06).
Rate leaves out a grid adjuster (Maple Run: +0.25% at the 85% LTC cap).
Recourse or completion guaranty wrong for the product (CORE-DOC-01 to -03).
Issued before the State Law Table check or OFAC screen (CORE-BP-03; CORE-KYC-01).
documents.input_rule: The term sheet is an output, not a source. Its numbers must be recomputed from the source documents before approval.
documents.data_needed: None: all terms are in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Construction contract or GMP summary
documents.what_it_is: The contract between owner and general contractor, or a summary of its price, scope and risk terms.
documents.producer: Owner and general contractor; reviewed by the lender's construction consultant and counsel.

format.description: Standard-form owner-contractor agreement, or a lender's one-page GMP summary of it.
references: AIA A102 (cost of the work plus a fee, with a guaranteed maximum price) and A101 (stipulated sum) [VERIFY: AIA Contract Documents; aiacontracts.com; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Contract sum or GMP; fee; general conditions
Contractor's consent to assignment to the lender
planted_defects: GMP excludes work the budget assumes is in the contract, so the budget has a gap.
Contractor is an affiliate of the borrower and this is not disclosed.
No payment and performance bond and no GMP (COM-CON-11).
Completion date falls after loan maturity or after the interest reserve runs out.
Unsigned, or dated after closing.
documents.deal_facts: Capstone not yet authored.
documents.input_rule: Hard costs come from the signed contract plus approved change orders. The borrower's budget is checked against it; the contract controls.
documents.data_needed: Whole document, once the capstone deal is authored.

documents.name: Hard and soft cost budget
documents.what_it_is: Line-item budget for the project: land, hard costs, soft costs, contingency, interest reserve, and who funds each.
documents.producer: Borrower or developer; checked by the lender's construction consultant (plan and cost review).

format.description: Sources and uses table with a line-item budget, often in the same lines as the schedule of values.
references: Line-item budget against a schedule of values is market practice [VERIFY: OCC Comptroller's Handbook, CRE Lending v2.0, 'Underwriting ADC Loans'; cited in needs analysis; not yet checked here]

fields_to_read: Land at cost and at appraised value
Soft costs: design, permits, legal, insurance, taxes, financing fees
Equity and loan funding by line; equity-first order
planted_defects: Contingency below 10% of hard costs, or computed on total cost (RES-GU-05; MF-CON-04; COM-CON-04).
Interest reserve missing, or sized at the note rate where COM-CON-06 needs strike + spread.
Land carried at contract price above appraised value (COM-CON-01).
Soft costs missing: builder's risk, property taxes during construction.
Developer fee counted as borrower equity.
documents.deal_facts: Rehab variant, Maple Run: hard costs $90,000; contingency $9,000; permits $1,000; total $100,000. Capstone not yet authored.
documents.input_rule: Land is the lower of cost and appraised value (COM-CON-01). Hard costs tie to the contract (DOC-15). Contingency is tested on hard costs only.
documents.data_needed: Capstone budget. Maple Run rehab budget exists.

documents.name: Construction schedule
documents.what_it_is: The contractor's timeline from permits to certificate of occupancy, with the expected draw curve.
documents.producer: General contractor; reviewed by the construction consultant.

format.description: Gantt or critical-path schedule with milestones and a monthly draw forecast.
references: No standard form; critical-path scheduling is industry practice [VERIFY: industry practice; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Substantial completion and certificate of occupancy
planted_defects: Completion falls after maturity, so an extension is assumed from day one.
First construction draw scheduled before permits are issued (RES-GU-04).
Draw curve front-loads spending, so the 60% average outstanding assumption fails (MF-CON-05; COM-CON-06).
No float on the critical path.
Leasing income starts before the certificate of occupancy.
documents.deal_facts: Capstone not yet authored.
documents.input_rule: The interest reserve uses the policy's 60% average outstanding. The schedule tests whether that holds; it does not replace it.
documents.data_needed: Whole document, once the capstone deal is authored.

documents.name: Builder background report
documents.what_it_is: The lender's check on the general contractor: license, insurance, record, liens, litigation and capacity.
documents.producer: Lender's credit staff or construction consultant, from public records and references.

format.description: Short report or checklist with license lookup, insurance certificate, project list and search results.
references: Contractor licensing is state law [VERIFY: Ohio, North Carolina and Indiana contractor licensing boards; not yet checked]
General liability evidence on ACORD 25 [VERIFY: ACORD forms FAQ; acord.org; checked 22 Nov 2026 via search summary]

fields_to_read: General liability and workers' compensation evidence
Years in business; completed projects of similar size
Mechanics' liens filed by subcontractors on past jobs
planted_defects: License expired, or for a different trade or state.
Several subcontractor liens on recent jobs, a sign the builder pays late.
Builder owned by a guarantor's relative (related party), not disclosed.
Liability insurance lapsed between the certificate date and closing.
Project several times larger than any the builder has finished.
documents.deal_facts: Capstone not yet authored.
documents.input_rule: Not a formula input. A gate for RES-GU-10, MF-CON-04 and COM-CON-11.
documents.data_needed: Whole document, once the capstone deal is authored.

documents.name: Title commitment
documents.what_it_is: The title insurer's promise to issue a lender's policy once listed requirements are met, subject to listed exceptions.
documents.producer: Title insurer or its agent.

format.description: ALTA Commitment for Title Insurance: Schedule A, Schedule B Part I (Requirements), Schedule B Part II (Exceptions).
references: ALTA Commitment for Title Insurance, 2021 v. 01.00 (07-01-2021); not valid without its notice, conditions and schedules [VERIFY: ALTA 2021 Commitment form, Florida OIR filed copy; checked 22 Nov 2026]
Endorsements named in policy: ALTA 32-series, ALTA 33 at each draw, ALTA 14 for other future advances (CORE-CLS-06) [VERIFY: ALTA endorsement forms; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Proposed insured lender and policy amount
Schedule B-I: payoffs, deeds, authority documents, lien releases
Schedule B-II: standard exceptions, taxes, easements, recorded leases, liens, judgments
planted_defects: Policy amount equals the initial funding, not the full commitment (CORE-CLS-06; Maple Run $340,000, not $240,000).
A mechanics' lien or judgment in B-II with no matching release in B-I.
Vested owner is not the seller on the contract, or took title weeks ago at a lower price.
Proposed insured or borrower name differs from the operating agreement.
Standard survey exception left in although a survey was ordered.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run closing costs $9,000 include title. Policy amounts must equal commitments: $340,000; $5,140,000; $3,520,000.
documents.input_rule: The deed history in the commitment is checked against the purchase contract (DOC-05). Where they differ, the recorded record controls and the gap is a finding.
documents.data_needed: Schedules for each deal. None in the Running Deals tab.

documents.name: Survey
documents.what_it_is: A licensed surveyor's drawing of the boundaries, improvements, easements and encroachments.
documents.producer: Licensed land surveyor, certified to the lender and title insurer.

format.description: Income property: ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey with chosen Table A items. 1-4 units: often a boundary survey, or none.
references: 2026 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys, effective 23 Feb 2026 [VERIFY: alta.org; read via law-firm summaries, primary text not opened; checked 22 Nov 2026]
Residential product table requires title, survey and flood for some products (Model Credit Policy, residential table)

fields_to_read: Certification parties and title commitment number
Zoning setbacks and parking count, where ordered
planted_defects: Certification omits the lender or cites a different commitment.
Legal description or area differs from Schedule A.
An encroachment on the drawing is not an exception in Schedule B-II.
Survey flood zone differs from the flood determination.
Old field date; newer improvements missing.

documents.input_rule: Derived document: it reports results; it is never an input source. Inputs come from the rent roll, T-12 and note (section 4).
documents.data_needed: A fictional buyer eligibility sheet (coverage review open item 2).

documents.name: Portfolio concentration report
documents.what_it_is: The portfolio by bucket (state, product, sponsor) against each limit, with headroom.
documents.producer: Credit administration, monthly (CORE-CONC-07).

format.description: Table by bucket: commitment, share, limit, headroom.
references: Supervisory CRE concentration screens [VERIFY: OCC Bulletin 2006-46; cited in C14 blueprint as opened]

planted_defects: Uses balances, not commitments.
A sponsor's affiliated entities not combined.
Pipeline loan not added before the share is tested.
Breached bucket not sent to committee.
documents.deal_facts: Commitments: Cedar Court $5,140,000; Birchwood $3,520,000; Maple Run $340,000.
documents.input_rule: Commitments, not funded balances (CORE-CONC-02).
documents.data_needed: A fictional portfolio around the three deals.

documents.name: Business-purpose, non-occupancy and use-of-proceeds certification
documents.what_it_is: A statement signed by the borrower and every guarantor. It says the loan is for business purposes and no guarantor or relative will occupy the property. On a cash-out refinance it states the use of proceeds.
documents.producer: Lender's form, signed by the borrower and each guarantor before closing. The closer checks signatures and dates; the underwriter tests it against the file.

format.description: One- or two-page lender form with a business-purpose statement, an occupancy statement and, for cash-out, a proceeds table. No industry standard form.
references: Purpose test it supports: Reg Z business-purpose exemption [VERIFY: 12 CFR 1026.3(a) and comment 3(a)-4; checked 18 Nov 2026 per Model Credit Policy CORE-BP-01]

fields_to_read: Borrower entity name and every guarantor's name and signature
Signature dates against the closing date
Occupancy statement covering guarantors and relatives
Cash-out only: use-of-proceeds lines and the personal-use total
Property address as shown on IDs and bills
planted_defects: One guarantor has not signed it (CORE-BP-01).
It is dated after the closing date.
The proceeds table puts more than half of cash-out to personal use (CORE-BP-04).
A utility bill or the guarantor's ID shows the subject address, contradicting the occupancy statement (CORE-BP-02).
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: both guarantors, Dana Reyes and Sam Okafor, sign the certifications. Dana lives elsewhere, and the property will be leased to an unrelated tenant. Cedar Court and Birchwood: signed certifications are closing conditions.
documents.input_rule: The certification supports purpose but never overrides contrary evidence. Any contradiction stops the file for the BSA officer (CORE-BP-02; CORE-KYC-07).
documents.data_needed: The lender's form text. Course Bible needs a template; cash-out what-if figures for C1 come from REG-03 (55% personal).

documents.name: Security instruments: mortgage or deed of trust, assignment of leases and rents, UCC-1
documents.what_it_is: The recorded documents that give the lender its lien on the real estate and the rents, and its filing on personal property.
documents.producer: Lender's counsel drafts; the borrower signs; the title agent records them and files the UCC-1.

format.description: State-form mortgage or deed of trust with a legal description, a separate or embedded assignment of leases and rents, and a UCC-1 financing statement.
references: Ohio and Indiana use mortgages; North Carolina uses deeds of trust with a power of sale [VERIFY: State Law Table SLT-OH-01, SLT-NC-01, SLT-IN-01; checked 20 Nov 2026]
UCC-1 national form [VERIFY: UCC 9-521 national financing statement form; not yet checked]

fields_to_read: Grantor matches the borrower entity exactly
Legal description matches the title commitment and survey
Secured amount covers the full commitment
Assignment of rents: present assignment and licence terms
UCC-1: debtor name, collateral description, filing office, lapse date
planted_defects: The grantor name differs from the borrower's legal name.
The legal description omits a parcel shown on the survey.
The UCC-1 is filed in the wrong state or office.
The secured amount covers only the initial advance, not future funding.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run (Ohio) and Birchwood Plaza (Indiana) take mortgages; Cedar Court (North Carolina) takes a deed of trust.
documents.input_rule: Trailing recorded originals are logged at funding and chased until received (CORE-CLS-05).
documents.data_needed: Legal descriptions and recording data for each deal.

documents.name: Guaranty agreements: payment, carve-out and completion guaranties; environmental indemnity
documents.what_it_is: The guarantor's signed promises to pay the loan, to pay losses from listed bad acts, to finish the work, and to cover environmental cost.
documents.producer: Lender's counsel drafts; each guarantor signs at closing.

format.description: Separate agreements per guarantor or one joint and several agreement, with a schedule of carve-outs and waivers.

fields_to_read: Each guarantor's name, signature and capacity
Carve-out list and springing full-recourse triggers
planted_defects: A 20% owner has not signed (CORE-BOR-03).
A non-owner spouse is required to sign though the guarantor qualifies alone (CORE-BOR-05).
No completion guaranty on a loan with future funding (CORE-DOC-03).
The carve-out list omits voluntary bankruptcy on a non-recourse bridge (CORE-DOC-02).
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: full-recourse guaranty from Dana and Sam, and a completion guaranty for the $100,000 rehab. Cedar Court: non-recourse with carve-outs, a completion guaranty for capex and an environmental indemnity.
documents.input_rule: Guaranty and remedy terms are checked against state deficiency and one-action rules before the term sheet (CORE-DOC-04).
documents.data_needed: Birchwood Plaza guaranty package is not stated in the deal file.

documents.name: Zoning report
documents.what_it_is: A third-party report on the property's zoning, permitted use, conformity and any open violations.
documents.producer: Zoning consultant ordered by the lender.

format.description: Report with the zoning district, permitted uses, required versus actual parking and setbacks, conformity status, rebuild rights and municipal letters.

fields_to_read: Legal conforming, legal nonconforming or illegal
planted_defects: The use is legal nonconforming and rebuild after a major casualty is limited.
Parking is short of the code requirement.
An open violation is noted but not addressed in the conditions.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: zoning report required (MF-GEN-08). Birchwood Plaza: zoning report required (COM-GEN-13).
documents.input_rule: Where the appraisal's highest and best use and the zoning report disagree, the zoning report controls on legal use; the difference is a finding.
documents.data_needed: Zoning facts for both deals.

documents.name: Site visit report with photos
documents.what_it_is: The lender's own record of a property visit, with dated photos and notes on condition, occupancy and the neighbourhood.
documents.producer: Originator, underwriter or third-party inspector.

format.description: Short form with checklist, narrative and dated, labelled photos.

fields_to_read: Match to the rent roll and the appraisal
planted_defects: Photos show personal belongings in a unit the file calls vacant.
Units on the rent roll as leased look empty.
Photos are undated or of a different property.
Staining or drums near a former service use are not followed up.
documents.deal_facts: No site visit facts in the deal file.
documents.input_rule: Contradictions with the certification go to the BSA officer (CORE-BP-02).
documents.data_needed: Visit notes and photo list for each deal. No policy rule requires a site visit (open item).

documents.name: Title date-down and UCC search
documents.what_it_is: An update of the title search to a later date, and a search of UCC filings against the borrower.
documents.producer: Title agent (date-down); search vendor or Secretary of State (UCC).

format.description: Date-down endorsement or letter listing new matters; UCC search report by debtor name and filing office.

fields_to_read: New liens, deeds or judgments since the last date
UCC filings by other lenders on rents or fixtures
planted_defects: A new mortgage to another lender appears.
A recorded claim of lien from a contractor appears before a draw.
A UCC filing by another lender covers rents.
documents.deal_facts: No date-down facts in the deal file; FRD-08 and FRD-10 items are what-ifs.
documents.input_rule: Each draw is insured as it funds (CORE-CLS-06); date-down with no new liens before each draw (CORE-SVC-05).
documents.data_needed: No rule requires a UCC search at origination (FRD-10 policy gap).

documents.name: Experience verification pack: prior settlement statements and deeds
documents.what_it_is: The evidence behind each project in the guarantor's track record.
documents.producer: Borrower supplies; the underwriter checks public deed records.

format.description: Schedule of projects with settlement statements, deeds and entity records for each.

fields_to_read: Guarantor's ownership share in the owning entity
Completion evidence: sale, refinance or 12 months held
planted_defects: The guarantor owned under 20% of a listed project (CORE-BOR-15).
A project completed more than 36 months ago is counted.
A deed shows a different owner with no link to the guarantor.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: Dana Reyes lists 7 projects; the 15% deal fails the 20% rule, so 6 count (Tier 2). Cedar Court: Marcus Hale lists 3 apartment properties; the 18-unit property owned 8% does not count.
documents.input_rule: Signed operating agreements, multiplied through layers, control ownership shares (CORE-BOR-03; CORE-BOR-15).
documents.data_needed: Project-level track records for each guarantor.

documents.name: Government ID
documents.what_it_is: A photo ID for each 20% owner, the control person, each guarantor and, on a purchase, the seller's signer.
documents.producer: Borrower parties; verified by the lender or closing agent.

format.description: Driver's licence or passport copy, with the verification record.

planted_defects: The ID address is the subject property (CORE-BP-02).
The ID has expired.
The name does not match the ownership chart.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: ID checks on both owners (CORE-KYC-01 to -03).
documents.input_rule: ID and OFAC results must name the same person as the ownership chart (CORE-KYC-02).
documents.data_needed: None beyond names in the deal file.

documents.name: AMC engagement letter
documents.what_it_is: The lender's order to an appraisal management company, naming the appraiser, the scope and the client.
documents.producer: Lender, through its AMC.

format.description: Engagement letter or order confirmation with the intended user, value types and fee.

fields_to_read: Client and intended user is the lender
Ordered through the AMC, not the borrower
planted_defects: The borrower or broker is named as client.
The appraiser was named by the broker.
The scope omits the after-repair value the loan sizes on.
documents.deal_facts: All three deals use lender-ordered appraisals (CORE-VAL-01).
documents.input_rule: Only an appraisal ordered under this letter may size a loan (CORE-VAL-01).
documents.data_needed: None.

documents.name: Rate-cap confirmation and collateral assignment
documents.what_it_is: The trade confirmation for the interest-rate cap and the assignment of its payments to the lender.
documents.producer: Cap counterparty, through the borrower's hedge adviser; assignment signed by the borrower and acknowledged by the counterparty.

format.description: Confirmation with notional, strike, index, term, premium and day count; separate assignment and acknowledgement.

planted_defects: The notional covers the funded balance, not the full commitment (D-CORE-30).
The term ends before loan maturity.
The counterparty is rated below A / A2 (MF-BR-09).
The assignment is not acknowledged by the counterparty.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: strike 4.25%, 24 months, notional $5,140,000, A-rated counterparty, cost $60,000 (course assumption). Birchwood Plaza: strike 4.25%, 24 months, notional $3,520,000, cost $40,000.
documents.input_rule: Coverage is tested at the higher of the note rate and strike plus spread (F-MF-12; MF-BR-09).
documents.data_needed: None.

documents.name: Plans, specifications and building permit
documents.what_it_is: The drawings and specifications for the work, and the municipal permit that allows it.
documents.producer: Architect or engineer; the municipality issues the permit.

format.description: Plan set and specification book; permit card or letter with scope and expiry.

fields_to_read: Plans match the budget and the contract
planted_defects: No permit before the first construction draw (RES-GU-04).
The permit scope is narrower than the budget.
The plan set differs from the one priced in the contract.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run: rehab budget includes $1,000 for permits; no structural work.
documents.input_rule: Permits are needed before the first construction draw; no exception (RES-GU-04).
documents.data_needed: Capstone plan set (CAP-01 not authored).

documents.name: Payoff letter
documents.what_it_is: A lender's statement of the amount needed to repay a loan in full on a stated date, with per diem after that date.
documents.producer: The servicer of the loan being repaid.

format.description: Letter with principal, accrued interest to the payoff date, fees, per diem and wire instructions.

planted_defects: Interest counts the payoff day (the payoff day does not count).
The exit fee is missing.
Wire instructions differ from those on file.
documents.deal_facts: Maple Run bridge payoff $340,000. Cedar Court bridge payoff $5,140,000 plus the 0.50% exit fee, $25,700: $5,165,700.
documents.input_rule: Interest runs up to but not including the payoff day.
documents.data_needed: None.

documents.name: Intercreditor agreement
documents.what_it_is: The agreement between the senior lender and a mezzanine lender on payment priority, cure rights and foreclosure on the pledged equity.
documents.producer: Counsel for both lenders.

format.description: Agreement with standstill, cure, purchase-option and transfer terms.

fields_to_read: Qualified transferee test for a mezzanine foreclosure
planted_defects: The mezzanine lender may foreclose without meeting a transferee test.
Cure periods run past the senior lender's remedies.
The senior loan cannot be modified without mezzanine consent.
documents.deal_facts: No running deal has mezzanine debt. Items use an exam-only fictional deal.
documents.input_rule: Senior documents and the intercreditor agreement decide who loses first.
documents.data_needed: An exam-only deal with mezzanine debt. No policy rule on mezzanine debt (open item).

documents.name: Take-out lender quote
documents.what_it_is: A refinance lender's indicative terms for the loan that will repay the bridge.
documents.producer: Agency, bank or life-company lender, often through a broker.

format.description: Term sheet or quote letter with rate, amortization, DSCR and LTV tests and its date.

planted_defects: The quote is stale.
The quote's DSCR uses pro forma income.
The rate omits a spread or fee the course adds.
documents.deal_facts: Cedar Court: agency 10-year fixed 6.55% as of 16 Nov 2026; the course sizes at the 7.25% grid rate. Birchwood Plaza: course take-out rate 7.75%.
documents.input_rule: The course sizes exits on its own stated rate, not the quote, where the policy says so (D-CORE-31).
documents.data_needed: None.

documents.name: Sources and uses with mezzanine debt and preferred equity
documents.what_it_is: A table of every source and every use of funds for a deal with a layered capital stack.
documents.producer: Sponsor or its adviser; the underwriter rebuilds it.

format.description: Two-column table, sources and uses, with totals that tie.

fields_to_read: Senior loan, mezzanine, preferred equity and common equity
planted_defects: Sources do not equal uses.
Preferred equity with a fixed return is shown as common equity.
Fees financed by the mezzanine loan are left out of combined leverage.
documents.deal_facts: No running deal has a layered stack. Items use an exam-only fictional deal.
documents.input_rule: Combined leverage counts every layer ahead of common equity.
documents.data_needed: An exam-only deal. No policy rule on combined leverage beyond F-MF-16 (open item).

documents.name: Buyer or warehouse eligibility sheet
documents.what_it_is: A capital partner's list of loans it will buy or finance, with advance rates and exclusions.
documents.producer: Loan buyer or warehouse lender.

format.description: Matrix of eligibility criteria, concentration limits and repurchase triggers.

planted_defects: A loan breaches one criterion but is listed as eligible.
A repurchase trigger is missed on a seasoned loan.
A concentration limit is breached by a new loan.
documents.deal_facts: Not authored. C14 O2 is blocked until the owner supplies it.
documents.input_rule: The partner's sheet binds the loan's financing; our policy binds approval.
documents.data_needed: Owner to supply a fictional sheet (open item 9). No figures are invented here.

documents.name: Market or feasibility study
documents.what_it_is: A study of demand, supply, rents or sale prices and absorption that tests whether a project can lease or sell as planned.
documents.producer: Market consultant, or the appraiser's market section.

format.description: Narrative report with supply pipeline, comparable rents or sales, absorption and a stabilization date.

fields_to_read: Sensitivity to rent and cap rate
planted_defects: Comparables are newer or in a stronger submarket.
The supply pipeline omits permitted projects.
Absorption assumes no competition.
documents.deal_facts: Capstone not authored.
documents.input_rule: Stabilized income for the back-door test comes from the study, cross-checked to the appraisal.
documents.data_needed: Capstone study. No policy rule on feasibility (theory map owner decision 3).

provenance_rules.deal_example: Marcus Hale's 8% stake does not count toward experience

open_items.detail: The ground-up capstone (CAP-01) is not authored. Recommendation (CCO review 6): RES-GU, a ground-up 1-4 unit spec build, because RES-GU-02 to -10 give a full rule set while MF-CON is teaching only. The owner decides before M4; DOC-15 to -18, -31 to -33, -56 and -62 wait on it.

Most documents need detail the Running Deals tab lacks: unit and suite rows, T-12 lines, comparables, title schedules, survey, insurable values, SREO, payment history. Each addition must tie to existing totals and be made in the Course Bible.
No policy age limit. Defects test name and status only until a rule exists.
No rule on when the lender must approve a change order. This is the C8 grey case in the exam template (7.4): the key is to condition the draw on credit-officer approval.
Only COM-CON-10 sets retainage. Residential and multifamily drafts treat retainage as a market concept.
No servicing-fee, remittance-date or deadline rule (C12 4.5 item 6). DOC-38 shows gross collections only.
DOC-38 needs a what-if in which Cedar Court is sold to a loan buyer. Confirm, or pick another deal.
DOC-44 needs a fictional buyer or warehouse eligibility sheet (coverage review item 2).
DOC-37 and DOC-45 need a small fictional portfolio around the three deals.
Reserved for C7. DOC-12 feeds them once defined.
No policy rule requires a site visit (DOC-50).
No rule on confirming the seller's identity on a purchase (FRD-11) or on netting seller credits (FRD-12).
No rule on subordinate debt (DOC-58, DOC-60). Items use exam-only deals.
REG-14 item 1 needs a stated basis for no Phase II, such as a no-further-action letter. Add it to the Course Bible or keep the item a what-if.
